hook.text: A fixed window can let 20 requests through in 10 seconds.
hook.say: A fixed window can let twenty requests through in ten seconds.

hook.text: The sliding window log is exact.
It keeps the time of every request.

log.text: Each key gets a sorted set in Redis.
First, drop the times older than 60 seconds.
log.say: First, drop the times older than sixty seconds.

log.text: Then count what's left. Already 10? Refuse.
log.say: Then count what's left. Already ten? Refuse.

log.text: If not, add this request's time, and let it through.

edge.text: Back to the edge: 10 requests at 0:55.
edge.say: Back to the edge: ten requests at fifty-five seconds.

edge.text: At 1:05, the window covers the last 60 seconds.
edge.say: At one minute and five seconds, the window covers the last sixty seconds.

edge.text: All 10 are still inside, so the request is refused.
edge.say: All ten are still inside, so the request is refused.

edge.text: Room opens at 1:55, when the first ones are a minute old.
edge.say: Room opens at one minute fifty-five, when the first ones are a minute old.

cost.text: The price: one entry for every request.
100 a minute for 10 million keys is about 16 gigabytes.
cost.say: A hundred a minute, for ten million keys, is about sixteen gigabytes.

cost.text: Use it for small, exact limits, like 5 logins a minute.
cost.say: Use it for small, exact limits, like five logins a minute.
